steps.title: A daily trust check, right up front
steps.narration: Every visit opens with one honest verdict: is today's data safe to rely on? You see that answer before anything else.
steps.point_out: The green banner confirming today's board is current.

steps.title: A leaderboard that admits what it doesn't know yet
steps.narration: Hundreds of stocks are ranked on leadership, entry quality, and risk — and every single score is honestly labeled 'Not yet proven' unless it has actually earned real trust.
steps.point_out: The small gray 'Not yet proven' chip sitting under every score, on every row.

steps.title: Searching narrows the list, never the honesty
steps.narration: Searching for a single company keeps every honesty label intact — nothing gets dressed up just because you're looking closer.
steps.point_out: The table narrows to matching rows as soon as you type.

steps.title: A stock pool that changes the way the real market does
steps.narration: The universe of tracked companies isn't fixed in stone — names join and leave on their real, historical dates, and the Methodology page explains exactly how.
steps.point_out: The Universe Selection section describing how membership is decided.

steps.title: How much can this stock actually hurt you?
steps.narration: Open any stock and see a plain-language risk breakdown: typical daily swings, overnight-gap danger, the worst multi-week stretch on record, and how close the price sits to the point the bullish case would break down.
steps.point_out: The 'Risk budget' card and its six tiles, each ranked against the rest of the market.

steps.title: Thirty years of honest price history
steps.narration: Flip on full history and the chart stretches back decades instead of months, clearly marking exactly where the older, deeper data begins.
steps.point_out: The chart's new caption, showing thousands of bars going back to 1996.

steps.title: Every tested idea keeps its full record
steps.narration: The Evidence page lists every trading idea ever tested, with its exact result and registration date — and now shows what actually holding it would have historically felt like, phase by phase.
steps.point_out: The drawdown-and-dry-spell table, broken down by market mood, with honest 'insufficient' labels wherever the sample is too thin.

steps.title: Inside the testing lab
steps.narration: The Factor Lab shows exactly which trading signals were tested, over which time horizons, and whether each one actually survived rigorous testing — never just a good-looking backtest.
steps.point_out: Every signal and horizon, honestly marked, spanning close to thirty years of history.

steps.title: Blended signals face the same bar
steps.narration: Combining multiple signals into one strategy doesn't earn it any shortcuts — every blend is held to the exact same honest standard.
steps.point_out: Each combination's own evidence status, right alongside the single-factor results.

steps.title: Every idea goes on record before it's tested
steps.narration: Before any hypothesis is even tested, it's written down in a public registry — so nobody can quietly try many ideas and only report the lucky one.
steps.point_out: The registry's list of every hypothesis, each with its own rationale.

steps.title: Failed ideas stay visible, never buried
steps.narration: Ideas that didn't hold up aren't quietly deleted — they're kept in a browsable record, so nobody wastes time re-testing something already known not to work.
steps.point_out: Rows marked permanently retired, right alongside their honest fail verdicts.

steps.title: A testing budget, spent in the open
steps.narration: Every statistical test spends a little of a shared, limited budget — and that budget is shown openly before it's spent, never explained away after the fact.
steps.point_out: How many tests have run so far, and how much budget is left.

steps.title: Checking the checker
steps.narration: Even the testing process itself gets audited, run against scrambled, fake data to prove it doesn't rubber-stamp things that aren't actually true.
steps.point_out: A tripwire check that honestly flags a real problem instead of hiding it.

steps.title: Your own watchlist
steps.narration: Beyond the main leaderboard, you can keep a personal watchlist of the names you care about most.
steps.point_out: The watchlist page, ready for your own picks.

steps.title: Adding a name to watch
steps.narration: Adding a company to the watchlist is as simple as typing its ticker.
steps.point_out: JNJ ready to be added.

steps.title: One click to confirm
steps.narration: A single click saves it to the list.
steps.point_out: JNJ now appears as a tracked name.

steps.title: A second, unrelated name
steps.narration: Adding a second company from a completely different part of the market sets up a much more useful comparison.
steps.point_out: XOM ready to join the watchlist.

steps.title: Two names, ready to compare
steps.narration: With two or more names saved, Trendora can start showing how they really relate to each other.
steps.point_out: Both tickers now sit together in the table.

steps.title: How concentrated is your watchlist, really?
steps.narration: A dedicated 'Concentration X-ray' shows how correlated your saved names actually are, how they cluster, and how many genuinely independent bets your list represents — described plainly, never as advice.
steps.point_out: The 'effective independent bets' headline and the correlation grid beneath it.

steps.title: The data behind it all
steps.narration: The Data Manager shows exactly how much history is on hand for every one of the hundreds of tracked companies, and how fresh it is.
steps.point_out: The dataset-coverage numbers and the availability legend.

steps.title: Guarding against silently bad data
steps.narration: If a data provider ever quietly revises history that was already locked in, Trendora catches the mismatch instead of trusting it blindly.
steps.point_out: The 'Live-vs-seed drift' card and its plain-language status line.
